items.text: Why is nuclear physics important?
items.ans: Nuclear physics is essential for understanding nuclear energy, nuclear medicine, and the fundamental structure of matter. It enables the development of nuclear power reactors and radioactive diagnostic techniques.

items.text: Introduce the branch of physics that studies the nucleus and its interactions.
items.ans: Nuclear physics is the branch of physics that deals with the study of the atomic nucleus and its constituent particles and interactions.
items.title: Introduction to Nuclear Physics

items.text: If a nucleus has 26 protons and 30 neutrons, what is its mass number and element?
items.ans: A = Z + N = 26 + 30 = 56, Element: Iron (Fe)

items.text: Compare the number of protons and neutrons in a stable nucleus for light elements.
items.ans: For light elements, the number of neutrons is approximately equal to the number of protons (N ≈ Z). The ratio N/Z increases for heavier stable nuclei.
steps: Ratio reaches ~1.5 for heavy stable nuclei

items.text: Explain the composition of the atomic nucleus.
items.ans: The atomic nucleus consists of protons and neutrons, collectively called nucleons. The number of protons defines the element.
items.title: Nuclear Composition

items.text: How many protons are in the nucleus of a carbon-14 atom?
items.ans: Carbon has Z = 6, so a carbon-14 atom has 6 protons. The mass number 14 includes 6 protons and 8 neutrons.

items.text: If an element has atomic number 92, how many protons and electrons does a neutral atom have?
items.ans: A neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons. Therefore, 92 protons and 92 electrons.

items.text: Explain the concept of atomic number and its significance.
items.ans: The atomic number Z equals the number of protons in the nucleus, which uniquely identifies the chemical element and determines its chemical properties.
items.title: Atomic Number

items.text: Uranium has atomic number 92. Name two isotopes of uranium and their mass numbers.
items.ans: Uranium-235 and Uranium-238, both have Z = 92 but A = 235 and A = 238 respectively.

items.text: If an element has 35 protons and 44 neutrons, and another isotope of the same element has 35 protons and 48 neutrons, compare their mass numbers.
items.ans: First isotope: A = 35 + 44 = 79. Second isotope: A = 35 + 48 = 83. The second has a larger mass number.

items.text: Explain the concept of isotopes and their significance.
items.ans: Isotopes are atoms of the same element (same number of protons) but with different numbers of neutrons, resulting in different mass numbers. They have nearly identical chemical properties but different physical properties.
items.title: Isotopes

items.text: Calculate the binding energy per nucleon for a nucleus with mass defect Δm = 0.008 u.
items.ans: E = Δm × c² = 0.008 × (931.5 MeV/u) = 7.452 MeV per nucleon

items.text: If the total binding energy of a nucleus is 1800 MeV and it has 60 nucleons, what is the binding energy per nucleon?
items.ans: E/A = 1800/60 = 30 MeV per nucleon

items.text: Calculate the binding energy given the mass defect.
items.ans: The nuclear binding energy is calculated using Einstein's equation E = Δm × c², where Δm is the mass defect (difference between the mass of individual nucleons and the actual nucleus mass).
items.title: Nuclear Binding Energy

items.text: If a source has an activity of 500 Bq, how many decays occur in 10 seconds?
items.ans: Decays = activity × time = 500 × 10 = 5000 decays

items.text: Explain the difference between alpha, beta, and gamma radiation.
items.ans: Alpha: 2 protons + 2 neutrons, low penetration. Beta: high-energy electron/positron, moderate penetration. Gamma: high-energy photon, high penetration.

items.text: Explain the concept of radioactive activity and its measurement.
items.ans: Radioactive activity is the spontaneous nuclear decay that emits radiation. It is measured in becquerel (Bq), where 1 Bq = 1 decay per second.
items.title: Radioactive Activity

items.text: Complete the nuclear reaction: ^{238}_{92}U + ^{1}_{0}n → ^{239}_{92}U → ?
Write the nuclear reaction for beta decay of ^{14}_{6}C.
Explain a nuclear reaction with an example.
items.ans: A nuclear reaction involves changes in the nucleus composition, where the number of nucleons and charge are conserved. Example: alpha decay where a nucleus emits an alpha particle.
steps: Conservation of mass number and charge
items.title: Nuclear Reaction

items.text: If a U-235 nucleus captures a neutron and fissions into Ba-141 and Kr-92, how many neutrons are released?
items.ans: U-236 → Ba-141 + Kr-92 + 3n, so 3 neutrons are released

items.text: Calculate the energy released in the fission of 1 kg of U-235, given that each fission releases about 200 MeV.
items.ans: Number of U-235 atoms in 1 kg = (1000 g)/(235 g/mol) × Avogadro's number ≈ 2.56×10^{24}. Total energy = 2.56×10^{24} × 200 MeV ≈ 5.12×10^{26} MeV ≈ 8.2×10^{13} J

items.text: Explain the nuclear fission process.
items.ans: Nuclear fission is the process where a heavy nucleus (like U-235) splits into two medium-mass nuclei when bombarded by a slow neutron, releasing additional neutrons and large amounts of energy.
steps: Heavy nucleus + neutron → fission products + neutrons + energy
items.title: Nuclear Fission

items.text: In the Sun's proton-proton chain, four protons fuse to form helium-2. If 10^38 fusions occur per second, what is the total energy released per second?
items.ans: Energy per fusion ≈ 26.7 MeV. Total power = 10^38 × 26.7 MeV/s ≈ 4.27×10^{39} MeV/s ≈ 6.8×10^{26} W

items.text: Compare the energy released per unit mass in fission vs fusion.
items.ans: Fusion of light elements releases significantly more energy per unit mass than fission of heavy elements (about 3-4 times more).
steps: Fusion ~3-4× energy per mass of fission
Mass difference per nucleon is larger for light nuclei

items.text: Explain the nuclear fusion process.
items.ans: Nuclear fusion is the process where two light nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus, releasing large amounts of energy. This is the process that powers the Sun (proton-proton chain reaction).
items.title: Nuclear Fusion

items.text: What are the main sources of natural background radiation?
items.ans: Main sources: cosmic radiation from space, terrestrial radiation from soil and rocks (especially radon), and internal radiation from potassium-40 in the body.

items.text: Explain the ALARA principle for radiation protection.
items.ans: ALARA = As Low As Reasonably Achievable. The principle states that radiation exposure should be kept as low as reasonably achievable, using time, distance, and shielding to minimize dose.

items.text: Explain the dual nature of nuclear radiation.
items.ans: Nuclear radiation has dual nature: significant benefits in medicine (diagnosis and treatment), energy production, and industry, but also risks including increased cancer risk, genetic damage, and environmental contamination if not properly managed.
items.title: Radiation Hazards and Benefits
